questions.question: What discount does Anthropic apply to cache reads versus the base input rate?
options: 90% off
25% off
50% off the base rate
75% off
questions.explanation: Anthropic's cache_control markers give a 90% discount on cache-hit input tokens versus the base rate, in exchange for a 25% write premium on the first request.

questions.question: Why must dynamic timestamps go below the cache breakpoint, not above it?
options: Timestamps confuse the tokenizer into splitting the surrounding system prompt into more tokens than expected
Timestamps cost more tokens per character than static text, so placing them early inflates the write premium
Caches only hit when the prefix is byte-identical; a changing timestamp breaks the match for everything after it
Anthropic explicitly rejects any cached block that contains a timestamp field, returning a validation error
questions.explanation: All three providers cache prefixes only. If any token differs between requests, everything after the first differing token is a miss -- so the stable parts (system prompt, tools, few-shots) must sit above any per-request variable like a timestamp.

questions.question: OpenAI's prompt caching is configured how?
options: Explicit cache_control markers placed on specific content blocks, the same mechanism Anthropic uses
Automatic prefix matching, with no configuration or explicit markers required from the developer
A CachedContent API you create ahead of time and reference by ID in each request, as Google's Gemini requires
A system-level flag toggled per project in a dashboard, separate from anything configured in the request body
questions.explanation: Unlike Anthropic's explicit cache_control markers or Google's CachedContent API, OpenAI detects matching prefixes automatically and applies the discount with zero code changes.

questions.question: For Anthropic, what write premium does the 1-hour extended TTL cost vs the 5-minute default?
options: Same as the 5-minute default, since the write premium is a fixed 25% no matter how long the cache is kept warm
2x the write premium, trading a higher upfront write cost for a cache that stays warm a full hour
4x the write premium, since extending the TTL from 5 minutes to 1 hour multiplies the base surcharge fourfold
No write premium at all for the 1-hour extended TTL, only the standard 90% discount applies on every read
questions.explanation: The 1-hour extended TTL doubles the write-side surcharge compared to the 5-minute default, trading a larger upfront cost for a longer window in which reads keep hitting the cache.

questions.question: How many reuses are needed to break even on Anthropic's 25% write premium?
options: 1 reuse
2 reuses
5 reuses
10 reuses
questions.explanation: With a 25% write premium and a 90% read discount, the second read alone recovers the extra cost paid on the write, and every reuse after that is close to pure savings.
